AMPSDEV-373 Preserve existing files when path validation fails

Validate Spring resource paths before conversion and retain input XML until all generated outputs are written successfully. Preflight existing ZIP and TAR destination components so a later symlink rejection cannot overwrite earlier files.

Share non-mutating path validation, add 14 regression cases, and clarify platform-specific path rules and partial-extraction limits in the changelog and Javadocs.

Validation: 114 tests passed, two Windows-only tests skipped on macOS, formatting checks passed, and both original security reproductions preserve existing files.

values.message:
AMPSDEV-373 Harden archive extraction and Spring Java transform against path traversal

Addresses the AMPS findings of the Bitbucket Data Center path traversal audit
(12 October 2026): A-005, A-006 and B-171 to B-178.

- Add PathConfinement, which confines writes to a root directory: it rejects
  absolute, drive-letter, UNC and escaping paths, and never traverses or writes
  through symbolic links or junctions below the root.
- ZipUtils refuses absolute entry names, symbolic links, hard links and other
  special files, validates every entry before writing anything, and writes
  through PathConfinement.
- TemplateUtil only loads templates by simple name and confines generated files
  to a root; SpringXmlToJavaConverter confines generated sources and spring.xml
  to the project's source and resource directories.
